newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-$0.50 lower - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-$0.50 lower - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were mostly steady to instances $0.50 per cwt lower, livestock dealers said.

Weakness was noted in the western Corn Belt, where Hormel Foods Corp's Fremont, Neb., hog slaughtering plant and its Austin, Minn., pork processing plant were closed for the Veterans Day holiday. Also, Quality Pork Processing Inc's hog slaughtering plant in Austin also was closed. The plant provides fresh pork to Hormel's Austin pork plant.
The reduced competition for hogs was pushing Iowa and southern Minnesota prices down $0.50, the dealers said.
Light sales were reported in Iowa and southern Minnesota at $52.00 to $52.50 per cwt in the country and $53.00 to $53.50 and possibly $54.00 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold steady at $51.50 to $53.00 in the country and $53.00 to $53.50 at plants, sources there said.
Indiana hog prices also were steady, at tops of $51.50 to $52.00 in the country and $52.50 to $53.00 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $48.50 to $49.50 in the country and $51.00 to $52.00 at plants.
Heavy lake-effect snow fell Sunday in northern Ohio, but was not hampering hog movement in the rest of the state.
